# lokl — Full Documentation

> lokl is a CLI/TUI tool for local development environment orchestration. It starts all your services (local processes and Docker containers) with a single command, provides automatic HTTPS with custom domains and auto-trusted certificates, and offers an interactive terminal UI. No mitmproxy, no nginx config, no browser extensions — just `lokl up`.

Source: https://shahin-bayat.github.io/lokl
GitHub: https://github.com/shahin-bayat/lokl

---

## Introduction

lokl is a CLI/TUI tool that allows developers to define their entire local development environment in a single configuration file.

### The Problem

Setting up a local development environment is painful:

- **Time-consuming** — New developers spend hours/days configuring their setup
- **Inconsistent** — "Works on my machine" syndrome
- **Complex HTTPS** — OAuth, cookies, CORS often require HTTPS with custom domains
- **Scattered config** — Docker Compose, npm scripts, env files, nginx configs everywhere

### The Solution

lokl provides:

1. **Single config file** — All services defined in `lokl.yaml`
2. **Automatic HTTPS** — Certificates generated and trusted for custom domains
3. **Process orchestration** — Health checks, dependencies, restart policies
4. **Interactive TUI** — Visual management of all services

### Key differentiators

- **vs Docker Compose**: lokl orchestrates both local processes and containers. Docker Compose only handles containers — you still need separate tooling (concurrently, npm-run-all) for local dev servers.
- **vs mitmproxy / nginx**: No manual proxy config. lokl generates and trusts certificates automatically. No browser extensions or system proxy settings needed.
- **vs concurrently / npm-run-all**: lokl adds HTTPS routing, health checks, dependency ordering, and a TUI on top of basic process management.

---

## Installation

### Requirements

- macOS or Linux (Windows not supported)
- Docker (only required if using container-based services)

### Homebrew (Recommended)

```bash
brew install shahin-bayat/tap/lokl
```

### One-liner Script

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shahin-bayat/lokl/main/install.sh | bash
```

This downloads the latest release and installs to `/usr/local/bin` (or `~/.local/bin` if no write access).

To install a specific version:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shahin-bayat/lokl/main/install.sh | bash -s -- v0.1.0
```

### Install from Source

Requires Go 1.23+:

```bash
go install github.com/shahin-bayat/lokl/cmd/lokl@latest
```

### Verify Installation

```bash
lokl --version
```

### Shell Completions

```bash
# Bash
lokl completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/lokl

# Zsh
lokl completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_lokl"

# Fish
lokl completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/lokl.fish
```

---

## Quick Start

### Auto-detect your project

```bash
cd your-project
lokl init
```

This scans your project, detects services, and generates a `lokl.yaml` config file.

### Or create manually

Create a `lokl.yaml` in your project root:

```yaml
name: my-project
version: "1"

proxy:
  domain: myproject.dev

services:
  app:
    command: pnpm dev
    port: 3000
```

### Start your environment

```bash
lokl up
```

This will:
1. Start all services
2. Generate HTTPS certificates
3. Configure local DNS
4. Open the interactive TUI

### DNS Setup (one-time)

```bash
sudo lokl dns setup
```

This adds entries to `/etc/hosts`.

### TUI Controls

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `j/k` | Navigate services |
| `s` | Start service |
| `x` | Stop service |
| `r` | Restart service |
| `l` | Toggle logs |
| `p` | Toggle proxy |
| `?` | Help modal |
| `q` | Quit |

---

## Configuration Reference

### Config File (`lokl.yaml`)

lokl uses a YAML configuration file, typically named `lokl.yaml`, to define your development environment.

#### Basic Structure

```yaml
name: my-project
version: "1"

proxy:
  domain: myproject.dev

env:
  NODE_ENV: development

services:
  service-name:
    command: ...
    port: ...
```

#### Top-level Fields

| Field | Required | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | Yes | Project name used for identification and DNS markers |
| `version` | No | Config version, currently `"1"` |
| `proxy.domain` | No | Base domain for HTTPS routing |
| `env` | No | Global environment variables inherited by all services |
| `services` | Yes | Map of service definitions |

---

### Services

Services are the core of your lokl configuration. Each service represents a process or container.

#### Command-based Services (local processes)

```yaml
services:
  frontend:
    command: pnpm dev
    path: apps/frontend
    port: 5173
```

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `command` | string | Shell command to run |
| `path` | string | Working directory (relative to config) |
| `port` | int | Port the service listens on |
| `env` | map | Environment variables |
| `env_file` | list | Paths to `.env` files to load |
| `depends_on` | list | Services to start first |
| `autostart` | bool | Start automatically (default: true) |
| `restart` | string | Restart policy: `no`, `always`, `on-failure` |

#### Container-based Services (Docker)

```yaml
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:16
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    port: 5432
    env:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: secret
    volumes:
      - ./data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
```

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `image` | string | Docker image |
| `command` | string or list | Shell command (string → `sh -c`) or exec args (list). Allowed with `image` to override the image's default command. |
| `ports` | list | Port mappings (`host:container`) |
| `port` | int | Host port for proxy routing and health checks |
| `env` | map | Environment variables |
| `env_file` | list | Paths to `.env` files to load |
| `volumes` | list | Volume mounts. `host:container` bind, `name:container` named, or bare `/container/path` anonymous (masks dir from outer bind, e.g. `vendor/`, `node_modules/`). |
| `subdomain` | string | Subdomain for proxy routing |
| `depends_on` | list | Services to start first |
| `health` | object | Health check configuration |
| `autostart` | bool | Start automatically (default: true) |

#### Dependencies

```yaml
services:
  api:
    command: pnpm dev
    depends_on:
      - db
      - redis

  db:
    image: postgres:16

  redis:
    image: redis:7
```

#### Health Checks

HTTP check (`health.path`) for web services:

```yaml
services:
  api:
    command: pnpm dev
    port: 3000
    health:
      path: /health
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
```

Exec check (`health.command`) for data services without HTTP endpoints:

```yaml
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:16
    health:
      command: "pg_isready -U myapp"   # string → sh -c wrap
      interval: 2s
      timeout: 1s
      retries: 10

  cache:
    image: redis:7
    health:
      command: ["redis-cli", "ping"]   # array → exec directly (no shell)
      interval: 1s
      retries: 5
```

`health.path` and `health.command` are mutually exclusive — use one or the other.

#### Overriding a container's command

`command` is allowed alongside `image`. It overrides the image's default `CMD` while preserving `ENTRYPOINT` — matching `docker run image cmd...` and Docker Compose's `command:` field.

```yaml
services:
  api:
    image: node:20
    command: "npm run dev"          # string → sh -c inside the container
  worker:
    image: node:20
    command: ["node", "worker.js"]  # list → direct exec, no shell
```

**Caveat:** images with an `ENTRYPOINT` (e.g. `python`, `node`, `postgres`) prepend it to the command. Shell-form `command: "script.py"` on a `python` image becomes `python /bin/sh -c "script.py"` — use the list form or a custom image when this matters.

**Requirement for shell form:** the image must contain `/bin/sh` (most do; `scratch` and some distroless images do not).

#### Container Networking

All containers in a lokl project share a bridge network named `lokl-{project-name}`.
Containers can reach each other using the service name as hostname:

```yaml
services:
  api:
    image: myapp:latest
    env:
      DB_HOST: db        # resolves to the "db" container
      REDIS_HOST: cache  # resolves to the "cache" container
    depends_on:
      - db
      - cache
  db:
    image: postgres:16
    health:
      command: "pg_isready -U myapp"
      retries: 10
  cache:
    image: redis:7
    health:
      command: ["redis-cli", "ping"]
      retries: 5
```

The network is created on `lokl up` and removed on `lokl down` (or when the process exits).

#### Environment Variables

Load from `.env` files:

```yaml
env_file:
  - .env

services:
  api:
    env_file:
      - .env.local
```

Variable interpolation using host environment:

```yaml
services:
  api:
    env:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://${DB_USER}:${DB_PASS}@localhost:5432/mydb
```

---

### Proxy & HTTPS

lokl includes a built-in reverse proxy with automatic HTTPS.

#### How It Works

1. **Certificate Generation** — lokl generates self-signed certificates for your domain
2. **Trust Store** — Certificates are added to your system trust store (no browser warnings)
3. **DNS** — Entries added to `/etc/hosts` for local resolution
4. **Routing** — Requests proxied to the appropriate service based on subdomain

#### Subdomains

```yaml
services:
  frontend:
    port: 5173
    subdomain: app      # → https://app.myproject.dev

  api:
    port: 3000
    subdomain: api      # → https://api.myproject.dev
```

#### Root Domain

A service without a subdomain gets the root domain:

```yaml
services:
  main:
    port: 3000
    # No subdomain → https://myproject.dev
```

#### Path-based Routing

Multiple services can share a subdomain using path prefixes:

```yaml
services:
  api:
    port: 3000
    subdomain: app
    rewrite:
      strip_prefix: /api

  frontend:
    port: 5173
    subdomain: app
    # → https://app.myproject.dev/api → api service
    # → https://app.myproject.dev/* → frontend service
```

#### Strip Prefix and Fallback

```yaml
services:
  api:
    port: 3000
    subdomain: api
    rewrite:
      strip_prefix: /v1        # Strip /v1 before forwarding
      fallback: /index.html    # SPA fallback for 404s
```

---

## CLI Reference

### lokl up

Start all services defined in your config file.

```bash
lokl up [flags]
```

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `-c, --config` | Config file path (default: `lokl.yaml`) |
| `-d, --detach` | Run without TUI (background mode) |

Examples:
```bash
lokl up                    # Start with TUI
lokl up --detach           # Start in background (no TUI)
lokl up -c custom.yaml     # Use custom config
```

### lokl down

Stop all services. Reads the lock file and kills service processes by process group.

```bash
lokl down [flags]
```

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `-c, --config` | Config file path (default: `lokl.yaml`) |

Works even if the lokl process was killed (e.g., terminal closed). Useful for cleaning up orphaned processes.

### lokl init

Scan your project and generate a `lokl.yaml` configuration file.

```bash
lokl init
```

Currently supports Node.js projects (monorepos and single-app). Detects pnpm, yarn, npm, bun. Infers ports from script flags and known tool defaults (vite: 5173, next: 3000).

### lokl validate

Check your config file for errors without starting any services.

```bash
lokl validate [flags]
```

Checks: YAML syntax, required fields, port conflicts, circular dependencies, env file resolution, Docker port mapping format.

Useful in CI:
```yaml
- name: Validate lokl config
  run: lokl validate
```

### lokl dns setup / remove

```bash
sudo lokl dns setup    # Add /etc/hosts entries
sudo lokl dns remove   # Remove /etc/hosts entries
```

Adds entries like:
```
# lokl:my-project
127.0.0.1 myproject.dev
127.0.0.1 app.myproject.dev
# lokl:my-project:end
```

Requires sudo. lokl only modifies entries within its own markers.

---

## Complete example (real-world multi-service app)

```yaml
name: my-app
version: "1"

proxy:
  domain: myapp.dev

env:
  NODE_ENV: development

services:
  frontend:
    command: pnpm dev
    path: apps/frontend
    port: 5173
    subdomain: app
    depends_on:
      - api

  api:
    command: go run ./cmd/server
    path: services/api
    port: 8080
    subdomain: api
    health:
      path: /health
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
    env:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://postgres:secret@localhost:5432/myapp
    env_file:
      - .env.local
    depends_on:
      - db
      - redis

  worker:
    command: go run ./cmd/worker
    path: services/worker
    env_file:
      - .env.local
    depends_on:
      - db

  db:
    image: postgres:16
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    port: 5432
    env:
      POSTGRES_DB: myapp
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: secret
    volumes:
      - ./data/postgres:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    health:
      command: "pg_isready -U postgres"
      interval: 2s
      retries: 10

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    ports:
      - "6379:6379"
    port: 6379
    health:
      command: ["redis-cli", "ping"]
      retries: 5
```

After `sudo lokl dns setup` and `lokl up`:
- `https://app.myapp.dev` → frontend (Vite dev server)
- `https://api.myapp.dev` → Go API
- PostgreSQL on localhost:5432
- Redis on localhost:6379
- Worker process started after DB is ready
